subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw add a fail-closed response-gate API, and which semantics should own mandatory tool accounting, validator trust, retry/fallback behavior, audit records, and plugin policy boundaries?
rationale: The request changes a security-sensitive final-response boundary plus plugin API/config behavior, and automation cannot safely choose those product and trust semantics.

options.title: Design a core/plugin responseGate API
options.body: Approve a versioned runtime seam for mandatory-tool ledgers, typed validators, fail-closed finalization, bounded retries/fallbacks, and auditable decisions while leaving domain policies to plugins or ClawHub.

options.title: Keep only adjacent hooks
options.body: Treat pre-tool hooks, message cancellation, and plugin output filtering as the supported policy surfaces and close or defer this broader response-gate request.

options.title: Split a narrower first milestone
options.body: Start with one smaller approved seam, such as a mandatory-tool ledger or final-action approval envelope, before committing to the full two-phase response protocol.

recommendation.title: Design a core/plugin responseGate API
recommendation.body: Approve a versioned runtime seam for mandatory-tool ledgers, typed validators, fail-closed finalization, bounded retries/fallbacks, and auditable decisions while leaving domain policies to plugins or ClawHub.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision centers on the plugin hook/API seam introduced in before_agent_finalize history.
